Electro-Magnetic Railway Pt.4.Author: Bunco
Electro-Magnetic Railway Pt.4.StartDialogue:
Good news, friend!.
The breech and rails are a perfect match.
I've even ran some dry fire tests and everything seems to work perfectly.
Now, for the sake of everyone here, I'd rather not leech any more of the precious little power we have.
That means, the next step is for you to nab a compatible power supply.
And it just so happens I might be able to save you the trouble of looking for one.
Or rather, he can.
Greetings, scav. Let me cut right to it.
You need a piece of our tech, and I need win in the Swamps.
The math is simple. You take care of our problem, and you get your tech.
Fresh off the assembly line. No bullshit, no tricks.
If that sounds acceptable, here are the details of what I need you to do.
Until next time.

Alright friend. Next up is the cooling system. 
Without it, you'd be able to fire three times before the whole thing starts to overheat.
My contact at the Eurasians has no more work to be done, so we're on our own here.
He did tip me off that the Mech Trenches might be a good place to start looking, however.
I think you understand the rest.
Good luck.

Electro-Magnetic Railway Pt.6.StartDialogue:
Hello again.
We're making good progress. The gun can fire, but for the sake of usability we're still missing some components.
Most important of which is the control system. The brain of this gun.

Some legs and an armature structure, namely.

Bunco's Bounties Pt.1.StartDialogue:
Remember what goes well with water?
I need you to spill not water for Bunco... but blood.
Are you thirsty like me? Help the scavs. Go to Scorched, and sip some Europan blood.

Bunco's Bounties Pt.2.StartDialogue:
You're back so soon? My crew and I missed your tales.
We know you can kill. But are you skilled against the different forces above?
Prove it. Spill the synth-blood of the Euruskans, and let us smell it on your hands.
Leave for Scrapyard at once.

Bunco's Bounties Pt.3.StartDialogue:
Ravenous, are we?
The final test of your combat worthiness, is against what I think are the deadliest foe. Go to the Frozen Swamp, and let the rivers flow with Eurasian nanofluid.

Electro-Magnetic Railway Pt.8.StartDialogue:
Our project is coming along nicely! Look at this beauty.
We ran out of material to reinforce the frame... as you can imagine, this is not a part we can compromise quality on.
Unfortunately, the best and safest way to put this part together, are with prefabricated components.
..and an alarm system associated with rapid reaction forces.
...guarded by possible turrets...
And these components... they are found in a secure bunker in Scorched...

In Search of Vex.Author: Slade
In Search of Vex.StartDialogue:
I've got a job for anyone willing to take it on.
We just lost one of our own, a scav by the name o' Vex.
He was out prospectin' for parts in the downtown ruins of Babel.
If not... well, just make sure nothin' important falls into the wrong hands.
If you can find Vex, bring him back safe and sound.

Silencing the Whispering Ghost.Author: Luca
Silencing the Whispering Ghost.StartDialogue:
Scav, we've had reports of a rogue marksman - a Euruskan taking out our people from a distance.
They're called 'The Whispering Ghost'.
Find out who's behind that name, and take them down. Can you handle this?

Scav, our medics have been stumped by this new illness sweeping through our ranks.
We need organic materials. Tissue samples.
Get me what you can from the affected Euruskans. Discreetly, of course.
I'm counting on your... flexibility in acquiring these samples.

Listen, I've got a request from one of our medics.

Break through the lock, get the goods and come back to me.

You look like someone I can trust with a personal job.
There's a Scav who's been asking about getting something back from the shanty - his family heirloom, an old knife.
It's probably just a hunk of metal to anyone else, but to him... it means something.
It must be in a container, bring it to me and I'll make sure you're paid.

We can't afford for Euruskans or anyone else to catch wind of this. Can you do it quietly?

Another Scav, eager for credits and oblivious to the dangers that lurk in every alley.

Lost Angels' Lowdown.StartDialogue:

Be cautious, Scav... this city is a powder keg, waiting to be ignited.

Shifting Tide Pt.2.Author: Slade
Shifting Tide Pt.2.StartDialogue:
Alright, we got wind of somethin' big through Caspian, but we need information.
His chatter's got our ears perked up about a new crew that split from the Water Thieves.
Find out what this new crew's all about, who their leader is, and where they're operatin'.
Here's the thing: Caspian mentioned this laptop that's been passed around among the water thieves.

Shifting Tide Pt.3.Author: Slade
Shifting Tide Pt.3.StartDialogue:
We now know Riptide's got his hideout rigged up tight in that old sewer system.
 Problem is, we can't just walk in - no power means no way in...
I got some news for you: there's a collapsed administration buildin' in the Downtown zone with technical plans buried in its rubble.
You're gonna have to navigate through that mess and see if you can find schematics of the sewer system.

Shifting Tide Pt.4.Author: Slade
Shifting Tide Pt.4.StartDialogue:
We need to get our hands on some water from Riptide's stash. Problem is, it's not exactly accessible.
The technical plans you found show there's a lever down in the Underground Cemetery.
If you can find that lever and flip it, we should be able to power up access to their hidden water cache.
It won't give us direct entry into the sewers, but it'll get us closer.

Shifting Tide Pt.5.Author: Slade
Shifting Tide Pt.5.StartDialogue:
You've got access to the sewers, but now you're gonna have to get inside Riptide's hideout without gettin' yourself killed.
I don't know what kind of crew Riptide's put together down there, but i bet they won't give up their stash without a fight.

Altitude Adjustment.Description: Infiltrate the old police station in Downtown Lost Angels and sabotage the helicopter fuel storage on its rooftop.
Altitude Adjustment.Author: Luca
Altitude Adjustment.StartDialogue:
Listen, we've got a chance to cripple Eurasia's air support in Downtown Lost Angels.
Intel suggests they refuel their choppers on the rooftop of an old police station.
I'm not going to sugarcoat it, this is a high-risk mission.
But if you can sabotage their fuel storage, it'll be a major blow to their operations. You in?
Altitude Adjustment.EndDialogue:

Objectives.Text: Destroy the Fuel Tank in Downtown

Communication Breakdown.Description: Infiltrate the shantytown in Downtown and sabotage Europa's communication antennas to disrupting their ability to coordinate.
Communication Breakdown.Author: Kane
Communication Breakdown.StartDialogue:
Scav, we've received intel that Europa's been setting up antennas for their communication networks in the Downtown district.
If you can take them out, it'll be a significant blow to their coordination and planning.
You're the best I've got for the job. Get in and get it done.
Communication Breakdown.EndDialogue:

Cracked Open.Description: Extract the hard drives from the Exos deployed in Downtown, giving Euruska access to valuable intel.
Cracked Open.Author: Владелец
Cracked Open.StartDialogue:
Alright, listen. We need hard drives from the Exos they deployed in Downtown.
They've got tech that could give us an edge on those Europa fools.
I don't care how you get them, just bring me what's on those drives.
You'll be rewarded well... Can I count on you, Scav?
Cracked Open.EndDialogue:

Psycho on the Loose.Description: Track down and neutralize the sadistic Europan EOD officer who has been terrorizing the Scavs in Downtown.
Psycho on the Loose.Author: Slade
Psycho on the Loose.StartDialogue:
Listen, you know how Europa's been gettin' bolder?
Well, it's 'cause they got one of their own EOD officers goin' around huntin' us Scavs and causin' chaos wherever he goes.
We're talkin' about the worst kind of psychopath. Someone who takes pleasure in hurtin' innocent people.
We need you to find out where he's hidin', and put a stop to this mess once and for all.
The camp under the elevated highway is your best bet.
Psycho on the Loose.EndDialogue:

HIDDEN GET THE CHOPPER.Author: Luca
HIDDEN GET THE CHOPPER.StartDialogue:
Alright, listen up, Scav. We've got a high-priority target on our hands, an Ultrahind MX!
It's a hunter-killer unit with a special loadout that's been wreaking havoc in Downtown.
I need you to create enough chaos in the area to draw it out, and then take it down.
This is not going to be easy, you'll need to think on your feet if you want to eliminate this thing. Can I count on you?

Guts and All.Author: Slade
Guts and All.StartDialogue:
Glad you made it, scav.
Bunco's intent on throwin' the bunch of you out…
but him and I have found a mutual understanding…
for now.
You stay, you work.
You don’t… well…
dead weight doesn't live long.
Get yourself familiar. 
Check out the terminals and ready room—you'll be using them often.
Come back when you’ve got your bearings.

Preparations.StartDialogue:
You’re getting ahead of yourself. 
But if you ain't prepared…
you ain't coming back.
I want you to meet some of the locals—Heisenburg, and Bunco. 
Heisenburg’ll keep you breathing.
Bunco’ll buy your teeth if you let him.
Buy a small medkit from Heisenburg, and grab a box of surplus 5.45x39mm for that east block antique of yours from Bunco.
Come back when you're kitted up.

Labyrinth.Description: The tunnels are a scav's best friend.
Labyrinth.Author: Slade
Labyrinth.StartDialogue:
Look at you.
Almost convincing. 
I think it's time for your first run. 
You're headed to the tunnels.
The place was built by machine minds we'll never understand. 
Not meant for you or me—but what in this world ever was?
Go in.
Find your way out.
If the place doesn’t fold you in half, we’ll talk about real work.

Blue Gold.Description: Slade wants to share with you the grave importance of water.
Blue Gold.Author: Slade
Blue Gold.StartDialogue:
Thirst hit you yet?
It will.
Water’s the only thing left worth killing over.
Not since those bastards camped out in the Frozen Swamp started controlling the supply.
See for yourself.
Check the water tank at the Innards—
That's our future running dry.
Bring back a barrel.
Carry it yourself.
You'll need an open bin on your rig to hold 'em.
No water, no Innards.
No Innards… no you.

Stashed Away.Author: Slade
Stashed Away.StartDialogue:
Listen close.
This place isn’t safe.
It just hasn’t been taken yet.
Bunco's got a line on the group working out of the Frozen Swamp.
Water skimmers.
They'll bleed you dry just for a drop.
Water that ain't nano-polluted doesn't come easy.
Makes folks desperate.
Makes 'em do evil things.
There's a place in the Innards.
Hidden.
I stash things there.
Find it, will you?
It's in the tunnel entrance, not too far from the quest terminal.
If things go bad…
we’ll want somewhere that isn’t obvious.

This Will Burn.Author: Slade
This Will Burn.StartDialogue:
The surface calls, scav. Are you prepared?
Enter the tunnels. 
Find a route to Scorched Enclave or Ashen Mesa.
Both’ll try to kill you.
Just different flavors.
Get your feet wet and try not to catch a bullet. 
I'll be here if you get back.

Objectives.Text: Travel to Scorched Enclave or Ashen Mesa via tunnel A

Thirsty Work.Description: Slade thinks you're ready to move faster.
Thirsty Work.Author: Slade
Thirsty Work.StartDialogue:
You been mapping the tunnels? Tracking your routes?
Let me see what you got.
Not terrible.
You’re starting to think.
Once you've scoped a route, it's easier to go back, you know? 
Thirsty work, though. 
Pack water. For longer routes you may need a drone, too.
Bunco says velocity wins.
Prove him right.

Bin Pigs.Author: Slade
Bin Pigs.StartDialogue:
You hauling anything worth a damn yet?
Or just burning through water for sport?
Bunco thinks you're just another tunnel rancher. 
Bring something back that proves him wrong.
Or don’t come back.
Bin Pigs.EndDialogue:

Seek and Destroy.Author: Slade
Seek and Destroy.StartDialogue:
You pay attention to the war?
Didn’t think so.
You should.
There’s money in it.
Made contact with my Europa contact. He has a job for us. The Eurasian forces are giving 'em hell at the Enclave and they're looking for options.
You've been reliable.
I want you to take the contract.
Eliminate six Eurasian units.
—tip the scales, if only a little.
And check your targets before you shoot, huh? Won't do us any good if you start fraggin' his boys.
Now get out there.

Steel on High.Author: Kane
Steel on High.StartDialogue:
Insipid filth. 
Did you believe Eurasia would suffer your opportunism?
Incensed as I am, you are something that I cannot kill. Not forever.
Raze one den of detrivores—another takes its place by sunrise.
It is revolting.
Vermin are persistent.
So instead—you will serve.
Destroy three Europan drones.
Bring me proof.
Delay… and I will collapse this hole you call shelter.

Violence of Action.Author: Kane
Violence of Action.StartDialogue:
Underfeeder.
Have you observed a Eurasian Runner? Ceaseless. Never tiring.
Much unlike you scavengers. So frail. So... metabolic.
You want more work?
Prove to me you can match their speed.
Bring everything to bear.
I'll be watching.

Extract from Scorched Enclave in 90 seconds or less

Surface Tension.Description: Kane is prepared to give you a worthy task.
Surface Tension.Author: Kane
Surface Tension.StartDialogue:
You require water.
Predictable.
Europans hoard it.
Like all weak things, they clutch resources they cannot defend.
There is a bunker.
Find it.
Take everything.
Surface Tension.EndDialogue:

Europans hoard it.

Objectives.Text: Access the locked bunker on Scorched Enclave

Kane's Favored.Description: Kane is wary of you—only but for now.
Kane's Favored.Author: Kane
Kane's Favored.StartDialogue:
You persist.
Why?
Your body is inadequate.
Your lifespan negligible.
And yet—you continue.
Serve Eurasia.
Break the Europan insects.
Earn something resembling advancement.

Go Home, Conscript.StartDialogue:
Ah, the ravening hyena. Looking for scraps?
Very well.
The Europan conscript. 
Tired. 
Sullen. 
A mere data point to the AI Judges that forsake them.
Their morale is fractured.
Exploit it.
Kill eight.
Bring me their IFF chips.
I prefer verification.

Bunco's comin' around, but he's still wary.
Out here, reputation is counted in runs survived.
Stay frosty, scav.
Keep gettin' out there—there's still much to learn.
The Hobo King.EndDialogue:

Objectives.Text: Reach prestige level 5 with your active scav

Run the Mesa.Description: Slade's mystery contact has another job for you.
Run the Mesa.Author: Slade
Run the Mesa.StartDialogue:
How's working for Kane?
You're still breathing, so that's good.
I knew you had it handled.
Bunco seems pleased too, but he'd never admit it.
Working for the Eurasia has its benefits,
but appearing too partisan puts a target on our back.
So we balance it.
I reached out to our Europa contact.
He's got a job, and I need you on it.
Go to the Ashen Mesa.
Scope the place out and extract.
Look.
Don’t linger.
Run the Mesa.EndDialogue:

Burst Transmission.StartDialogue:
So.
You’re the one who’s been dropping our people on the west flank.
What a waste.
Lucky for you,
I don't do grudges.
Three Radar Walkers roam the Scorched Enclave.
Command put them there for battlefield telemetry, but the interference is bad enough that somebody has to go in and collect the data by hand.
My crew is busy at the moment.
So that leaves you.
Hack 'em for me and we'll call things even, all right?

Eye on the Sky.StartDialogue:

I’m aware of Kane.
I know how he operates.
Pain and misery for his own people,
and plenty left over for us.
Anyway, I need a favor.
We had a radar array at the Enclave that helped keep our boys alive.
I need you to get it back online.
Find the array's generator and get it fueled.
Everyone appreciates an early warning.

Triggerman.StartDialogue:
How's your aim, scav?
Because if it’s bad, you’re already dead—
you just don’t know it yet.
Show me you can hit something that moves.
Then we talk real contracts.

Gun Nutty.StartDialogue:

It's a statement.
Some people like the vintage classics, and others jerk off to front line footage.
Either way, I’ve got something for you.
I've got some old-school collimators the hardest bastards of the 21st used to run.
The right mod can make all the difference. 
Take care of that weapon and it'll take care of you.
Kit up with some premium attachments and end some Eurasia Soldiers for me.
You won't regret it.

Roll Deep.Author: Slade
Roll Deep.StartDialogue:
You’ve been going out alone.
That works—until it doesn’t.
There are a thousand ways to die in Lost Angels.
Half of them start with thinking you can manage by yourself.
That’s why you get the locals to watch your back.
Plenty of scavs will sign on for a cut.
I’ll cover it this time.
Consider it… insurance.

Zaibatsu work.
Bodies turned into platforms.
Kept just alive enough to function.

Put eight of them down.

They don’t hesitate.
 Neither should you.

About you.
About what’s coming in on your runs.

Build Mother Courage's body rack.StartDialogue:
The workshop doors slide open.
Steel screams against steel.
Inside—
everything has changed.
The tarp is gone.
The walls have been stripped.
Half the room has been demolished.
Support columns now disappear into fresh concrete footings.
A crawler crane sits where workbenches used to be.
Tank suspension arms hang from chains.
The place looks less like a garage...
and more like the beginning of a cathedral.
Octogirl is standing twenty meters away with a welding mask raised onto her forehead.
She's staring at a framework of black steel rising toward the ceiling.
She doesn't notice you've entered.
(Scav): ...
What are you doing?
Without turning...
(Octo): Building a support frame.
(Scav): For what?
(Octo): For her digestive tract.
(Scav): ...
You decided.
She looks exhausted.
Not guilty.
Not excited.
Resolved.
(Scav): After everything we talked about?
(Octo): After everything.
(Scav): You said we'd destroy her.
(Octo): I know.
(Scav): You changed your mind.
(Octo): No.
I lost an argument.
(Scav): With who?
A tiny smile.
(Octo): Myself.
(Octo): I tried.
I boxed her up.
Cut the power.
Welded the restraints shut.
I even drew up demolition charges.
She laughs quietly.
(Octo): Then I spent three nights, sitting with the weight of it.
She looks up.
The framework towers overhead.
(Octo): Curiosity is a drug.
(Octo): It's an itch.
One you can't scratch.
One that keeps spreading until eventually...
you're rebuilding a classified biomechanical horror because you need to know why someone designed vertebrae strong enough to carry grief.
The scav looks toward Madonna.
Her head remains suspended in its cradle.
Eyes closed.
Silent.
(Scav): This is insane.
(Octo): Of course.
(Scav): Then stop.
Octogirl places both hands on the steel beam.
Feels its weight.
(Octo): I can't.
(Octo): If I walk away now...
I'll spend the rest of my life wondering.
Every machine I fix.
Every implant I install.
Every soldier I put back together.
I'll wonder whether I left the answer buried under a tarp because I was afraid.
(Octo): Fear isn't enough.
Progress has always been purchased with someone else's nightmares.
And the progress is worth it.
The scav walks the perimeter.
The frame is enormous.
Far too enormous.
(Scav): How much is this going to hold?
Octogirl checks a clipboard.
(Octo): If my estimates are right...
two hundred and eighty metric tons.
(Scav): For a digestive organ?
She nods.
Neither of them notices that Madonna's eyes have opened.
Just a fraction.
Watching.
Listening.
Waiting.
(Scav): You're negotiating with an atomic bomb.
Octogirl smiles.
(Octo): No.
She looks up at the frame.
(Octo): Yesterday I was.
She picks up the welder.
The arc ignites.
White light fills the room.
(Octo): Today...
We let it burn.
The torch hisses.
Steel joins steel.
Another piece locked into place.
Another irreversible decision.
Over the crackling of the weld—
a voice.
Almost drowned out.
(Madonna): Curiosity is how civilizations reproduce.
The welding stops.
Octogirl doesn't turn around.
She already knows the voice is awake.
(Octo): ...
I know.
(Madonna): So is regret.
The torch reignites.
Brighter than before.
Octogirl turns to the Scav.
(Octogirl): please bring me what I need to finish this.
No one speaks again.

Build Mother Courage's Upper Torso.StartDialogue:
The workshop is quiet.
Madonna watches from her cradle.
The unfinished support frame looms behind her.
Octogirl is studying a collection of grainy reconnaissance data on her screen.
Another Mother Courage.
Different unit.
Different battlefield.
Different war.
Same impossible anatomy.
She doesn't look up when you enter.
(Scav): What now?
(Octo): I need another one.
The scav doesn't answer.
Looks at the image.
Then at the head hanging from the crane.
Then back again.
(Scav): No.
Octogirl nods.
(Octo): That was my first answer too.
A long silence.
(Scav): You're talking about killing another one.
(Octo): Yes.
(Scav): To rebuild this one.
She finally looks up.
(Octo): To understand this one.
She sighs.
(Octo): The head survived.
The memory architecture didn't.
The lower vault is unique.
No fabrication marks.
(Octo): No replacement parts.
No service manuals.
Whoever built them never intended repairs.
Only recovery.
She taps the image.
(Octo): That means every surviving Mother Courage...
is carrying the only spare parts that exist.
The scav looks sick.
(Scav): You want me to tear one apart.
(Octo): I want you to destroy it.
Then recover the torso before Eurasia does.
Another silence.
(Scav): After everything we endured last time.
(Madonna): No.
Both turn.
(Madonna): It is organ donation.
The room goes completely still.
Octogirl closes her eyes.
(Octo): ....
The digestive tract should remain intact.
The retention organs.
The vault.
(Octo): If I can recover it...
I can rebuild the lower body.
I can stabilize the memory substrate.
I can see how she stores souls, 
and maybe then, 
we could have more.
(Scav): And if we don't?
Octogirl’s lenses click.
(Octo): Then we walk away.
Burn the workshop.
Forget any of this happened.
(Octo): But if we're going to continue...
there isn't another way.
Madonna's eyes never leave the scav.
(Madonna): She is correct.
(Madonna): The dead have always repaired the living.
The scav looks between them.
One obsessed.
One impossibly calm.
For the first time...
they sound like they're on the same side.
The thought is more frightening than the mission itself.
Octogirl quietly hands over the operation file.
(Octo): Plant the charges.
Bring down the torso.
Mark it for drone extraction.
Dont fucking die.

(Octo): Dont fucking die.

Not with life.
With synchronization.
Octogirl sits in front of a wall of diagnostics.
The display has stopped changing.
(Scav): It's still searching.
Octogirl nods.
Lenses fixed on the monitor.
(Octo): The vault completed compiling the fireteam data.
It rebuilt their shared memory lattice.
Their emotional indexing.
Their combat telemetry.
Everything.
(Octo): Except purpose.
The scav waits.
(Octo): Every squad organizes itself around one mind.
The Glue.
(Octo): Every recovery fireteam has an Assault Officer.
Close-quarters specialist.
The first through the breach.
The last one out.
The one that carved the path everyone else followed.
(Octo): By the time they earn that mantle...
they've butchered thousands.
Enough killing that the rest of the squad stops questioning where to stand.
They just follow.
She enlarges a tactical diagram.
Five nodes orbiting a sixth.
The center remains dark.
(Octo): Without her...
the memories exist.
But they don't know where they belong.
Madonna speaks from the cradle.
Eyes still closed.
(Madonna): The constellation has no north.
Octogirl slowly pulls another file onto the screen.
Grainy reconnaissance.
A woman.
Tall.
Heavy officer plating.
Eurasian command mantle.
Designation:
ASSAULT OFFICER — SQUAD LEAD
Status:
ACTIVE
(Scav): She's still alive. 
Still hunting us.
(Octo): ...
Barely.
Satellite imagery appears.
The officer moving alone through ruined streets.
(Octo): She's been searching the battle site for weeks. 
Carving up unlucky scavs.
(Scav): Better them than us.
Octogirl nods.
She quietly powers down the monitor.
(Octo): I don't need her alive.
The scav says nothing.
(Octo): I need her mnemonic index.
That's where the synchronization routines live.
She hesitates.
(Octo): When you bring it back...
this machine will stop looking.
The scav stares at the suspended vault.
Its slow rhythmic pulse.
Patient.
Expectant.
(Scav): And then?
Octogirl looks toward Madonna.
Madonna looks back.
Neither answers.
Finally—
Madonna speaks.
(Madonna): Then...
they will remember they are dead.
And I can start drinking in new memories.
Octogirl hands over the operation file.
(Octo): Find Assault Officers.
Recover mnemonic cores from them.
Bring it back.
And if they asks you where their squad is...
She trails off.
Unable to finish.
Madonna finishes for her.
(Madonna): Tell her...
they've been waiting.

HIDDEN Tobacco Journey Pt 1.Author: Slade
HIDDEN Tobacco Journey Pt 1.StartDialogue:
*flicks cigarette at your feet*. Its LORDOSS. With 'O's. You think I don't understand your childish Europan slur. It was given to me. The ones that found me, -saved me-... if you can call this *gestures to himself* saved... they gave me this name. I wear it with gratitude, even though I've come to understand it was... inspired... by my condition.
*looks around for a cigarette* thinking about the past always hurts. To have lived my life meant doing great things, and some terrible things. Things I'd rather not have to think about constantly. But they seep back now and again.
Listen. All this reminiscing... is starting to not feel so good. But you can help me endure it if I had some basic cigarettes. You just wasted my last one. *tilts head back and stares at the ceiling* Don't look at me like that. I know you don't work for free.
Bring me 3 packs of Dogboro Cigs
And I will reward you a large rig bin and 10,000 credits
